name: Demon, Kargamog
body:
Kargamog Demon
CR 7

This stout, horned demon is engulfed in flames. Its massive hands are almost as threatening as the roaring ball of flame it has drawn from its very body.

XP 3,200
CE Medium outsider (chaotic, demon, evil, extraplanar)
Init +6; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +14

DEFENSE

AC 21, touch 12, flat-footed 19 (+2 Dex, +9 natural)
hp 94 (9d10+45)
Fort +11, Ref +8, Will +5
Defensive Abilities fiery flesh; DR 5/cold iron and good; Immune electricity, fire, poison; Resist acid 10, cold 10; SR 18
Weaknesses vulnerable to cold

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee 2 slams +15 (1d6+5/19-20 plus 1d6 fire) and gore +14 (1d6+5 plus 1d6 fire)
Special Attacks detonate Spell-Like Abilities (CL 9th; concentration +12)

At will—fireball (DC 18)
3/day—dispel magic, heat metal (DC 15)
1/day—air walk, greater teleport (self plus 50 lbs. of objects only), summon (level 4, 1d3 brimoraks 50%)

STATISTICS

Str 21, Dex 14, Con 21, Int 14, Wis 15, Cha 16
Base Atk +9; CMB +14; CMD 26
Feats Ability Focus (fireball), Combat Casting, Improved Critical (slam), Improved Initiative, Weapon Focus (slam)
Skills Acrobatics +14, Bluff +15, Intimidate +15, Knowledge (engineering, planes) +14, Perception +14, Sense Motive +14, Stealth +14
Languages Abyssal, Celestial, Draconic, Ignan; telepathy 100 ft.

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Detonate (Su)

A kargamog can, as a standard action, explode in a 30-foot-radius burst that deals 8d6 points of fire damage (Reflex DC 19 for half). The save DC is Constitution-based.

Fiery Flesh (Su)

Any creature that hits a kargamog with a non-reach melee weapon is burned by its heat, taking 1d6 points of fire damage.

ECOLOGY

Environment any (Abyss)
Organization solitary, band (2–6), or platoon (7–16)
Treasure standard

Kargamogs are insular and self-concerned demons that live on island archipelagos located in all pockets of the Abyss that are filled with fire and lava. They bear a tangential relation to brimoraks and kalavakuses, sharing parts their origin with the former and appearance with the latter. Kargamogs form from the souls of pyromaniacs that wrought fiery destruction on a wide scale. No simple arsonists, examples of souls that now make up the ranks of kargamogs include renegade fire mages, warlords who scorched the very lands they ruled and conquered or military engineers with a burning passion for alchemical fire. Kargamogs are stout and extremely strong, boasting a prodigious pair of horns and powerful, overmuscled mitts that wouldn’t look out of place on an ogre. Physically, they are similar to a squished-down kalavakus with hoofed legs, red skin and a fire coming out of their very core that burns through their body, escaping through their eyes, nostrils, mouth and various fissures forming on their body. Not only are they constantly aflame and as such pose a risk to any who approach them in melee, they are also able to control these flames within them to a supernatural degree. The main ability which kargamogs use in combat and for which they are valued when drawn into demonic armies is their great skill at detonating their fire. They can explode at will and without any harm to themselves, scorching all foes around them. Combined with their natural toughness, it makes them excellent candidates as shock troops, charging down enemy lines and setting fire to their defenses, homes and very bodies. Kargamogs can also draw those flames out of their bodies and throw them, essentially giving them an unlimited, internal supply of fireballs, and a platoon of kargamogs can easily overwhelm a small army by relentlessly abusing this ability and raining fire upon enemy ranks until there is nothing left. This ability also makes them particularly useful at sieges or murderous raids, as they are able to quickly lay waste to buildings at a distance, scorching their inhabitants and flushing the survivors out.

For their part, kargamogs dislike such calling. While their love of fire and destruction is great, they are not traditionally social and rarely contact even other demons of their own volition. Moreover, they feel great unease when drawn far from their lava?flooded homes. Still, their opinion is rarely accounted for when powerful demons march to war, and some kargamogs learn to like the opportunities that such service grants them, destroying foreign land and burning it down and down again, until the very air is superheated and it starts to feel like home. Kargamogs are occasionally called by mortal spellcasters for their overwhelming destructive abilities. While they dislike such situations, they aren’t very prideful, and often consent to work for minor offerings as long as the task is short. They prefer gifts of magic that either controls fire or grants some form of protection against cold, and they always ensure that their fire does as much collateral damage as possible during their service.

An average kargamog is 5 feet tall and weighs 330 pounds.

This enormous orb of tough flesh and bony plate is dominated by a cavernous maw and a baleful, red eye. Countless shimmering soul gems pierce its hide, armoring their jailor.
